intuition: Two strings are anagrams when each character appears equally often in both. Count the characters in the first string, then consume one count for every character in the second. A missing count rejects the match. Equal lengths ensure no unused copies remain after a successful scan.

Count the characters in s, then consume one copy for every character read from t. If any count becomes negative, t requires more copies of that letter than s supplies, so equality is impossible. Check lengths first: strings with different total character counts cannot be rearrangements of each other.

After a same-length t finishes without a deficit, every supplied copy has been used. A positive leftover would require a negative count elsewhere to maintain the equal total, and that would already have been rejected. Thus no separate final all-zero scan is needed.
The dictionary implementation makes the invariant visible even though the allowed alphabet has only 26 letters; it would also work for a larger character alphabet.

For a larger Unicode alphabet, this dictionary compares code-point occurrence counts. A precomposed accented letter and a base letter followed by a combining mark can look identical but contain different code points. Supporting such visual equivalence would require an explicit normalization policy before counting; it is outside the lowercase English-letter contract.

steps: For anagram and nagaram, both lengths are 7, so continue.
Count s as a=3, n=1, g=1, r=1, m=1.
Consume the leading n of t, then a and g, reducing those counts without a deficit.
The next a reduces a to 1; r then reaches zero.
The final a and m reduce their counts to zero. Every requested copy was available.
Return true, because equal length and no negative counts establish matching occurrence counts.

codeNotes.note: Rearrangement cannot change the number of characters, so unequal lengths reject immediately.
Record occurrence count rather than just character presence.
A deficit means the second string requests a copy the first string does not contain.

keyDecision: Equal total length is necessary, but every individual character count must also match.
